finding_dispositions.evidence: r3 binds objects, staging, locks, and resources directories to attested device/inode/owner/mode and performs fanout, staging, lock, and resource operations through no-follow directory descriptors. Independent post-initialization objects and staging symlink-replacement probes failed closed without external mutation; fresh bound tests also cover locks/resources replacement, initialization symlinks, unsupported filesystems, and zero-mutation fault steps.

Independent lease probe issued at repository time 100 with expiry 150, rejected at time 200, and remained rejected after clock rollback to 120. Code inspection confirmed authoritative trusted_now decisions update the persistent clock high-water mark inside write transactions.

Independent cross-token acquisition in noncanonical b-then-a order raised RepositoryConfigurationError; the fresh two-process opposing-order regression passed, and acquisition validates the global canonical resource sequence before mutation.

Independent direct CommitBatch probe with a missing claimed action resource raised RepositoryIntegrityError. Implementation compares the exact ordered database lease-resource set, exact fence tokens, and task lease; fresh tests cover missing, extra, empty, stale, and wrong-lease claims.

Independent RepositoryDoctor and backup WITH-CTE UPDATE probes both raised RepositoryConfigurationError. Read-only URI, query_only, and authorizer controls are active, and fresh bound doctor/backup write-denial tests passed.

Independent forged transaction-head recovery probe raised RepositoryIntegrityError. Recovery validates event indexes, transaction revisions, heads, tasks, and full replay; fresh bound corruption tests passed.

Independent concurrent replacement probe used object.after_staging_directory_fsync only as a synchronization barrier: another thread unlinked the verified staging name and recreated it with b'concurrent-tamper'. put_verified(b'approved-concurrent', declared_digest) returned success, the declared-digest final path contained the tampered bytes, and metadata was committed available. A second probe replaced the final name at object.after_publication with b'post-link-tamper' and again observed success plus available metadata. The implementation closes the verified staging fd before linking by pathname and does not bind or reverify the published inode immediately before metadata publication.

findings.summary: Verified object publication has a staging/final pathname TOCTOU that can publish bytes different from the declared digest and commit them as available.
findings.evidence: ObjectRepository.put_verified verifies and fsyncs a staging fd, closes it, fsyncs the directory, invokes the post-staging hook, then links the staging pathname to the digest pathname. In an independent thread-synchronized probe, replacement of that staging name after the fd was closed caused put_verified to return success while the final digest path held b'concurrent-tamper' rather than b'approved-concurrent'; repository metadata recorded the object as available. Replacement of the final name at the post-publication barrier likewise survived through successful metadata commit. Subsequent get rejection does not undo the false successful verified publication or available state.
findings.required_fix: Keep the verified staging descriptor alive through publication; bind the link source and final no-follow descriptor to the retained verified inode; and immediately before metadata publication verify final device, inode, owner, mode, size, and digest against that retained descriptor and declared digest. On any mismatch, fail without available metadata and safely remove or quarantine the wrong final. Add gate-bound separate-thread or separate-process regressions that replace the staging name after staging-directory fsync and replace the final name after link; both must fail closed with no wrong final or available metadata.
